headline: Southborough advanced a $38 million Neary School renovation plan and navigated contentious Town Meeting warrant articles alongside tightening FY28 budget preparations.
synopsis: In October 2026, the Elementary School Building Committee voted to advance Option 3, an estimated $38 million addition and renovation plan for Neary Elementary School, after architects concluded a lower-cost $15 million option was unworkable under building codes. Town boards prepared for and debriefed Special Town Meeting, where voters backed Peninsula Trail footbridge funding and landfill water main connections, but rejected a two-family zoning amendment that fell short of a two-thirds majority. Municipal and school departments began drafting FY28 operating and capital budgets under fiscal pressure, preparing contingency plans and service cuts in case a Proposition 2 1/2 override fails. The Personnel Board adopted the 60th percentile of peer communities as the benchmark for a comprehensive compensation study, establishing an appeals panel to address pushback from department heads and staff. Meanwhile, major commercial reviews moved forward as the Planning Board extended its decision deadline on the 21 Coslin Drive Costco proposal.

top_items.title: Neary School $38M addition-renovation plan advanced
top_items.why: The Elementary School Building Committee voted 4-0 to advance Option 3 to schematic design after architects demonstrated that a $15 million cap left inadequate funding for essential systems.
top_items.body: Analysis from Tappé Architects revealed that a $15 million budget cap would leave only $5.8 million for direct construction after deducting the ongoing roof project, soft costs, and mandatory code compliance such as fire sprinklers and ADA upgrades. Because that scope could not address boilers, univents, or educational improvements, the committee voted to advance Option 3—a comprehensive addition and renovation project estimated at $38 million to $39.8 million—for detailed site and cost modeling.

top_items.title: Town-wide salary study adopts 60th percentile benchmark
top_items.why: The Personnel Board adopted the 60th percentile of peer communities for non-union municipal salaries and set a November 24 deadline for employee appeals.
top_items.body: Consultant MGT presented a draft Classification and Compensation Study proposing to expand the Salary Administration Plan from 9 to 12 grades aligned with regional peers. Following concerns from multiple department heads and staff over specific job gradings and titles, the board established a three-member review panel to evaluate written employee appeals before bringing final recommendations to Town Meeting.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge advanced to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Community Preservation Committee voted 3-2 to advance a $217,318 CPA funding request for the Peninsula Trail footbridge without proposed cuts.
top_items.body: Ahead of the October Special Town Meeting, the Community Preservation Committee decided against floating a floor amendment that would have stripped contingency funding, opting to keep the full $217,318 request on the warrant for the $428,550 footbridge. The Trails Committee coordinated public outreach and FAQ materials to address questions regarding Route 30 pedestrian safety, state MassTrails grant leverage, and overall costs.

top_items.title: Capital committee reviews $2.15M requests and bondable projects
top_items.why: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee evaluated $2.15 million in capital requests and up to $49 million in bondable projects for FY28.
top_items.body: Departments submitted FY28 requests that far exceed typical tax levy placeholders, led by Public Works fleet and water infrastructure, $710,000 in school facilities maintenance, and police equipment leases. The committee discussed scheduling joint sessions with the Select Board and Advisory Committee before Thanksgiving to establish financial parameters and evaluate bonding thresholds.

top_items.title: Costco warehouse hearing continued with deadline extended
top_items.why: The Planning Board extended its decision deadline to December 18, 2026, for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and gas station at 21 Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: With traffic peer reviews still in progress, the Planning Board voted unanimously to continue its public hearing for the Costco site plan and special permits to November 2 and formally extended its statutory decision deadline to December 18. The project faces extensive review over regional traffic congestion and Route 9 intersection impacts.

top_items.title: Teachers contract amended to align salaries with Algonquin
top_items.why: The Southborough School Committee voted 5-0 to approve collective bargaining amendments for Southborough Teachers Association Unit A.
top_items.body: The approved amendments modify retirement incentive provisions in Article 29 and update Article 22 to align Southborough's teacher salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027. School officials confirmed the agreement following executive session negotiations.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee recommends $240,000 for landfill water connections
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 6-0 to recommend Article 7, funding $240,000 from water retained earnings to connect two homes near the Parkerville landfill.
top_items.body: The committee confirmed with the Select Board that the town will pay the full cost of extending the water main and connecting the two residences from the street into the houses. The project aims to eliminate long-term contamination risks and state-mandated well testing following chemical detections in monitoring wells near the capped landfill.
